sentences: I measure the warp threads on the warping board before I thread them through the heddles.
I pass the shuttle back and forth across the loom to build up the weft rows.
I soak the cotton fabric in a dye bath and stir it for thirty minutes.
I lay the pattern pieces on the grainline and pin them before cutting the fabric.
I stitch a straight seam with the sewing machine and press it open with an iron.
I cast on sixty stitches and knit stockinette stitch in the round for the body.
I chain four stitches and join them into a ring to start the granny square.
I layer the quilt top, batting, and backing, then baste them with long stitches.
I thread the needle with six strands of floss and stitch a satin stitch leaf.
I agitate the wool fibers in warm soapy water until they bind into a dense mat.
I draft the wool fibers and twist them onto the spindle to make yarn.
I check the fabric's repeat and match the plaid lines at the seam.
I fold the raw edge twice and sew a narrow hem along the bottom.
I finish the seam allowances with a zigzag stitch to prevent fraying.
I unroll the bolt of fabric and measure two yards with a tape measure.
I cut along the selvage to remove the tightly woven edge before sewing.
I set the loom for a twill weave by threading heddles in a four-shaft pattern.
I burn a small sample of the yarn to check if it is cotton or polyester.
I count the threads per inch in the fabric to determine its thread count.
I wash the new fabric in hot water to preshrink it before cutting.
